'''Fudbalski klub Mačva Šabac''' ({{Lang-sr-Cyrl|Фудбалски клуб Мачва Шабац|lit=Football Club Mačva Šabac}}) is a Serbian professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Šabac]], which competes in the [[Serbian SuperLiga]].

One of the oldest football clubs in Serbia, their nickname is {{Lang|sr|Provincijski Urugvaj}} ({{lit|the provincial Uruguay}}), which was first used in 1927, when the [[Uruguay national football team]] were one of the best teams in the world, and due to local people and media comparing Mačva's style to that of the Uruguayan team, the main daily newspaper ''[[Politika]]'' consistently used the nickname {{Lang|sr|Provincijski Urugvaj}}.

In the period of [[Yugoslavia]], Mačva mostly played in the lower tiers of the football system but did spend two seasons in national top flight of [[Yugoslav First League|Yugoslavia]] in the [[1951 Yugoslav First League|1951]] and [[1952 Yugoslav First League|1952]] seasons. Afterwards, they would spend the next six decades in the Yugoslav lower-leagues but were a stable and respected lower-tier club in the country.

Mačva reached the [[Serbian SuperLiga]] for the first time ever in the [[2017–18 Serbian SuperLiga|2017–18 season]], returning to the top tier of Yugoslav/Serbian football for the first time in over six decades.<ref name="fkmacva_2020-07-31">{{Cite web|url=http://www.fkmacva.com/vesti/778/macva-u-subotu-docekuje-o/ |date=2020-07-31|title=Macva-Vesti|website=fkmacva.com|access-date=2020-07-31}}</ref>"}}
